payload.title: Blackwell Matrix Multiplication Part 2: Hardware Feature Optimization
payload.summary: Loop tiling, TMA loads, tcgen05 MMA with Tensor Memory, swizzle patterns for bank-conflict-free shared memory access, and TMA store — building from 5 TFLOPS to 293 TFLOPS on B200.

sections.heading: 1. Performance Roadmap
sections.gist: Focus on a specific matmul shape: A is M×K, B is K×N (transposed), C is M×N, with M=N=K=4096.

sections.heading: 2. Kernel 1: Loop Tiling
sections.gist: Loop tiling loads small blocks (tiles) into faster memory (shared memory), allowing the processor to execute all necessary computation on that block before returning to slow main memory.

sections.heading: 3. Kernel 2: TMA and Tensor Core
sections.gist: The Tensor Memory Accelerator (TMA) is a dedicated hardware unit introduced in Hopper for asynchronous data transfer between global and shared memory.

sections.heading: 4. Kernel 3: Swizzle
sections.gist: Shared memory consists of 32 consecutive 4-byte-wide banks.

sections.heading: 5. Kernel 4: Pack Output in SMEM + TMA Store
sections.gist: Previous kernel writes 4-byte stores (two BF16 values) — too granular given Blackwell's 32-byte maximum store width.

sections.heading: 6. Appendix: Descriptors
sections.gist: The shared memory descriptor encodes: - **LBO (Leading dimension Byte Offset)**: Bytes between adjacent core matrices along K (e.g., BM×16B = 1024B) - **SBO (Stride dimension Byte Offset)**: Bytes between adjacent core matrices along M/N (…

sections.heading: 7. Appendix: Swizzle Math
sections.gist: Given `Swizzle(bits, base, shift)`: extracts bits at positions [base+shift, base+shift+bits) as a mask, XORs with bits at positions [base, base+bits).
